prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a steep downward egocentric view of an outdoor lawn where the camera wearer (the only person present, facing forward and looking straight down) pushes a walk-behind lawn mower across five frames. Bright white to light-grey tones place the wearer's upper torso at 0.1–0.4 m below the head-mounted camera, both extended arms and hands gripping the mower handlebar within arm's reach at about 0.5–0.7 m in front and below, and the mower's grass catcher bag and engine deck further ahead on the ground at roughly 1.0–1.7 m from the camera (0.5–1.0 m ahead of the handlebar). Between the wearer's occluding torso and the handlebar, slightly darker grey shapes appear in alternating frames (left leg/foot in frames 1, 2, and 5; both knees/feet in frame 3; right leg in frame 4) at 0.8–1.4 m below the camera as the wearer walks forward while maintaining a constant distance to the mower, whose front edge is partly cropped at the top of the frame. Compared to RGB, the depth map clearly separates the vertical height gradient from the raised handlebar down the angled support rods to the mower body and ground plane, avoiding texture confusion from the patchy grass and mulch. However, the depth map is unreliable along the thin side cables/rods, which partially vanish into the dark ground depth, and around the flat grass background where subtle ground slopes are compressed into uniform near-black.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates the camera wearer's torso, arms, hands, and stepping legs at the bottom center (0.1–1.4 m from the camera, facing forward and looking down with no other people present) from the unlabelled black background lawn. Across all five frames, the wearer's left and right hands remain within arm's reach at 0.5–0.7 m, gripping the mower handlebar directly in front of the torso while the torso occludes most of the lower body except through the gap between the arms and handlebar. As the wearer walks forward with slight lateral sway and a slight leftward turn by frame 5, the map captures the changing shape of the gap between the arms and chest where the stepping legs and handlebar sit, while the top of the mower and bottom of the wearer's head remain partly out of view. While the segmentation mask makes the continuous silhouette boundary of the wearer's upper body and arms easier to see than in RGB, its semantic labels and object detections are highly unreliable under this steep egocentric angle. Specifically, it completely misses the lawn mower in frames 2, 3, and 5, misclassifies the mower deck and grass bag (~1.0–1.7 m ahead) as a "parking meter" and a tiny "person" fragment in frames 1 and 4, merges the handlebar into the "person" mask in frames 2–3, and mislabels the handlebar center as a "cell phone" in frame 5.
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders only two magenta 2D hand skeletons on a black background, corresponding to the camera wearer's left and right hands positioned within arm's reach at roughly 0.5–0.7 m in front of and below the downward-looking camera, spaced about 0.3–0.4 m apart left-to-right on the mower handlebar. Each hand skeleton shows the wrist at the outer lower corner and five curled fingers wrapping forward and inward around the angled grips, confirming the wearer faces forward behind the mower while no other people are in the scene. Across the five frames, the pair of hand skeletons shifts slightly upward in frames 2–3 and tilts slightly counter-clockwise (left hand higher, right hand lower) in frame 5, tracking the subtle handlebar angle and torso sway as the wearer walks forward. Compared to RGB, the magenta keypoints make the exact finger articulation, thumb placement, and symmetrical grip orientation immediately explicit without visual clutter from the handlebar or grass. However, the map is unreliable for full-body spatial understanding because it completely fails to detect the yellow body skeleton for the wearer's visible shoulders, elbows, torso, and stepping legs—which are heavily foreshortened and self-occluded from the head-mounted viewpoint—and provides no representation of the lawn mower or ground.
